partisan

PAR-tih-zun — starts like 'part'; a partisan sticks firmly to one part, or side. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Partisan is strongly favoring one side, party, or cause, often without willingness to consider other views.

The debate on the new law quickly turned partisan, with neither side willing to compromise.

Example

Two news channels give the same city council vote openly partisan coverage. One only interviews people who supported the measure and shows the crowd cheering. The other only interviews opponents and shows people protesting.

Each channel presents the story from only one side, refusing to show any balance. Unlike 'opinionated,' which just means having a personal opinion, partisan specifically means favoring one side over another, often at the expense of fairness.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

one-sided: One-sided describes anything that presents or favors just one side — a one-sided account, a one-sided match. Partisan is more specific: it means loyally favoring one party or organized side, especially in politics, often refusing to weigh the other side's views at all.

factional: Factional means driven by rival groups inside one larger organization — factions battling within a single party, church, or club. Partisan loyalty usually points outward, backing a whole party or side against its rivals rather than one clique inside it.

biased: Biased means unfairly tilted toward one side, whatever the cause — habit, friendship, self-interest — and often without the person even knowing it. Partisan slant is chosen and organized: a partisan speaker takes a side on purpose and defends that side's whole position.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

open-minded: willing to consider views different from your own

impartial: treating all sides fairly

Where it sits · how fierce the one-sided loyalty is

opinionated → partisan → fanatical

opinionated vs. partisan: Opinionated is weaker than partisan — having a strong opinion is personal, while being partisan means aligning firmly with an organized side or party.

fanatical vs. partisan: Fanatical is stronger than partisan: a partisan supporter favors one side, but a fanatical one refuses to hear even the smallest criticism of it.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — part-: part, side (Latin)

suffix — -isan: one who takes or belongs to (Italian/French)

Put it together: Latin pars/partem meant 'a part or side.' A partisan is literally someone who has firmly taken one part or side of a dispute rather than staying neutral.

Use the root in a new word: participate: Her essay asked whether any newspaper can truly be impartial.
